-  Cozy Living room, kitchen (with dishwasher), and shower with bathtub. 
Experience the “real” New York by staying in one of the hottest spots in the 5 boroughs.  Start your trip off right and get the best of both worlds without paying the high NYC tourist price tag! 

Located on a quiet street in the heart of Astoria, just minutes from the N, Q Train, right off 30th Ave, which is considered the hub of this vibrant neighborhood.  Walk up to Steinway Street for a plethora of authentic Middle Eastern restaurants, or experience the best of Astoria, with the best tasting Greek food found outside of Greece.  Astoria is a true example of a melting pot. 

Want to experience fabulous views of the city? Take a short walk to astoria park for some beautiful shots. 

Wanna stay in and cook an  international meal?

- You won’t have any problems doing that here; Astoria has great grocery stores (some 24/7) with a large international selection.
  
Do you need to get something from the drug store in the middle of the night?
 
-You’re covered, there is a 24 hour Duane Read right up the street.  
. Do you think New York is intimidating or are you worried about staying in a safe neighborhood?
 
-Astoria is one of the safest neighborhoods in the five boroughs. I’ve lived here for 6 years and have always felt safe walking at any hour, day or night. 

 You’ll enjoy waking up to chirping birds, while still having the New York City playground in your backyard. Enjoy strolling past the many 24 hour fresh fruit stands on your way out the door, or on your way home. You’ll get a plush apartment without the NYC price tag plus the bonus of a knowledgeable NYC Insider! 

 Did you know, Astoria is also a film hub in new york? Ever wonder where the famed 30 Rock or Law & Order is filmed? Well it’s right here in this neighborhood at Kaufman Astoria studios. In addition to this, Astoria has become popular for location shoots, and you’re likely to find a movie being filmed on your way home. How cool is that! 

  Are you looking for a memorable experience beyond that of a typical run of the mill vacation? 

You’ve found it here! Get the benefits of staying with a local: access to a knowledgeable local living in the apartment, which will be able to provide valuable tips to make your experience  beyond that of a run of the mill vacation/ tour.

name: Charming room in unique apartment
summary: Private bedroom in a very cozy apartment, a ten minute walk from the subway, near busses, parks, great restaurants and bars in both Greenpoint and Williamsburg. Quick trip into Manhattan or Queens
space: This truly is a completely unique apartment in one of the best parts of NYC. With beautiful woodwork and solid construction we've tried to make a very comfortable room for you to come home to during your stay in Brooklyn.
description:
This truly is a completely unique apartment in one of the best parts of NYC. With beautiful woodwork and solid construction we've tried to make a very comfortable room for you to come home to during your stay in Brooklyn. 

Feel free to use our well stocked kitchen if you'd like to cook. There is a grocery store around the corner and many small butchers, cheese shops and a Sunday Farmer's Market all within a block or two. We have several books and music, as well as a TV with Netflix, Hulu, etc... if you want a night in and even a piano for any musicians out there who care to play. Make yourself at home.

We can have as much or as little interaction as you'd like. We're happy to hang out and grab a couple beers or just give you recommendations for some of our favorite bars, restaurants, music venues, or parks nearby. We've been guests in other AirBnBs and have hosted so we know what it's like to be on both sides. All we ask is that you don't bring a party back to the house.

This is really one of the best neighborhoods in NYC. Just 2 blocks from a beautiful park with a great Farmer's Market, lots of restaurants, bars, shopping, etc... We're in Greenpoint but on the border of Williamsburg and very close to Long Island City Queens and Bushwick. You can be in Manhattan in 20 minutes but come home to a completely quiet home in a very friendly, very safe neighborhood.

We're a ten minute walk to the L train into Manhattan or the G train which will take you to other Brooklyn neighborhoods as well as into Queens. There are several busses and the East River Ferry is about a 15 minute walk if you care to try that out.

summary: A keyed elevator opens directly into this full floor apartment's spacious, well-lit living room and giant kitchen. A long hallway with a sitting area/sleeper sofa and small bedroom leads to 2  FULL bathrooms and 2 PLUS-sized bedrooms. TOTAL PRIVACY!
space:
Hi there! Thanks for taking a minute to read the description - it's a huge apartment with lots to offer in an incredible area of Manhattan. Please let me know if you have any questions!

QUICK OVERVIEW:
Bordering the Gramercy and Flatiron neighborhoods just north of Union Square and South of Madison Park, this loft-style building is centrally located to just about everything and offers tons of space and privacy. I just started sharing my apartment in October to help me cover the costs of starting a company. 
Just to be clear, there is one apartment per floor in my building and the elevator requires a key to operate (I will provide you with 2 sets). When you arrive at my floor, the door opens directly into the living room. Very cool!

This apartment is ideal for guests that wants to feel at home and stay in comfort. Whether you are a couple that values space and want to use the other bedrooms for guests or an office, or a group/family of 6 - 8 that want to stay together to have  more fun and save money as opposed to a hotel, this is the place for you!

NEW NEW NEW:
I just bought all new bedroom furniture, sheets, towels, pillows, 3 high-end queen mattresses, a sleeper sofa that has a pull out full-sized bed, and a high end queen sized air mattress (it's double the thickness - like having a box spring - and automatically adjusts the air pressure, making it an incredibly comfortable addition). So, if you include the air mattress, there are technically 5 beds (I listed 4). 
Of the 12 closets (yes, 12!), there are 6 empty closets for your belongings, 2 empty chests of drawers, and 2 clothes storage units, making it easy to move in and unpack your suitcase.

APARTMENT PERKS:
A high-end home theater surround sound system, hundreds of cable channels, HBO, Apple TV, Netflix, WiFi, a wireless land-line phone with free calls in the US, a chef's kitchen with large island and everything you need to cook a family-sized meal, wood floors throughout, a trash chute, laundry in the building, a roof you can venture out on for fresh air, high-end stereos in the back bedrooms and master bath that you can plug your phone into, a large desk with a 30" monitor that you can connect your laptop to in case you're required to work, and that's just the interior! Don't forgot to get out and enjoy NYC!

LAYOUT SPECIFICS: 
The apartment has really thick ceilings and floors that provide sound insulation from the neighbors, and the back rear bedrooms face the inside of the city block, making it quiet at night for sleeping. Additionally, the long hallway acts as a buffer and separates the 2 back bedrooms from the front common space. This is great if some guests  want to nap or sleep, while others can socialize or watch a movie without disturbing  one another. It's that big! (The unit is 90 feet long from front to back).

In the middle of the apartment there is a small bedroom; opposite the hallway from the bedroom is a nook with a full-size sleeper sofa. This bedroom is cozy and has an interior-facing window and sliding door, but is nothing unusual for New York size-wise. There is a large air conditioner / heater next to the bed on one side, an end table on the other, an in-wall fan to bring in fresh air, and enough space to change in privacy. This is actually my favorite place to sleep! The fans create enough white noise to drown out most noise outside of the room, and if you close the window curtain, it's pitch black!

Internet access is an added bonus during your stay.

This room sleeps 2 and is furnished with very comfortable queen-sized bed, coffee maker and small refrigerator.  WiFi is also included.  Use of the kitchen is not included, but I do provide a complimentary continental breakfast and with the refrigerator in the room, you can stock other simple things for yourself.. Since we are on the ground floor, there is some typical street noise of people passing by and in the summer it can be lively on the weekends.  But my guests have told me that they have found it quiet and peaceful. I have a small rabbit that lives here, Jenny, but he does not go into the part of the apartment where the guest room is located and so far, though I have had guests with allergies, they have not had any trouble or reactions to Jenny.  The apartment is centrally located - very close to 4 major subway lines,(20 minutes to midtown) 9 blocks from Central Park and 4 blocks from all of Harlem's most famous attractions: The Apollo Theater, The Studio Museum of Harlem, and the Abyssinian Baptist Church (a little further north, on 138th street.)  The neighborhood has great shopping, restaurants and several charming cafes nearby.  Please see my guidebook for more information on local places to eat .  I have lived in Harlem  for 10 years and I have found it to be safe, and that's saying a lot, as I walk around by myself at all hours and use the subway late at night. Quintessential brownstones line tree-trimmed sidewalks and local retailers and Italian eateries populate its cheerful main street. For a stroll or a stay, Carroll Gardens promises a healthy dose of Brooklyn's cool candor.
Carroll Gardens was settled by Irish Americans in the early 19th century and, in the mid-19th century, by Norwegian-Americans, who founded the Norwegian Seamens' Church, an imposing brownstone structure on the corner of First Place and Clinton Street that was once visited by the King of Norway during an official visit to the United States, and which still stands as a residential condominium.

space:
Need a place convenient to all locations, but away from the bustle of mid-town?

 When all you need is a place to crash while you explore the Big Apple, this is it.   The room maybe small, but comes with many amenities. Continental Breakfast included.

name: Private room in Harlem brownstone
space:
A huge, sunny room in a beautiful Harlem brownstone.  The room comes with a comfortable mattress, breakfast table, desk and computer, reading lamps, nice places to sit, and closet space.  Feel free to use the huge kitchen as well!  The floors are shiny hardwood and covered in pretty rugs.  Everything is clean, dusted, shined and smelling good.

The whole block is brownstones, and the room is on the third floor, with floor to ceiling windows and wide enough window sills to sit and enjoy the view below, but high enough from the ground to avoid the noise.

You're right by great public transportation here.  The express 2/3 trains are just blocks away, which will take you along the Upper West Side, to Times Square, through Wall Street and into Brooklyn.  The express A/D and the local B/C are also a short walk away, and will take you through the heart of Manhattan.

The walk to Central Park from the room is just half a mile.  You'll see the Harlem Meer and be near some of the prettiest hidden gardens in the whole park.  You'll also be near the Apollo Theater, Red Rooster Restaurant, Marcus Samuelsson's newest restaurant, and soul food faves like Amy Ruth's (which has the best mac and cheese ever!!)

Hope to meet you soon!

name: 3Br Duplex Near Columbia University
summary: Space-filled 3 bed/ 2 bath duplex apartment in Harlem, near Central Park and Columbia University. Thoroughly modernized since its construction in the early 1900s, The rooms are well furnished with everything needed to make you feel at home.
space:
Space-filled 3 bed/ 2 bath duplex apartment in Harlem, near Central Park and Columbia University. Thoroughly modernized since its construction in the early 1900s, The rooms are well furnished with everything needed to make you feel at home.

Make yourself at home in Harlem in this space-filled three bedroom / two bathroom duplex apartment, just 5 blocks north of Central Park. Situated on the upper two floors of a four-story walk-up building, this vacation rental benefits from skylights in the hall and bathroom of the fourth floor. Thoroughly modernized since its construction in 1900, this brownstone offers a video buzzer/intercom system to screen and allow in visitors, as well as a combination washer/dryer, always a valuable amenity when traveling.

The rooms of this apartment are well furnished with everything needed to make you feel at home, yet the clean lines and simplicity of the furniture emphasizes the open space of the rooms. You'll find hardwood floors throughout both levels, except of course for the tiled bathrooms. You also have exposed brick walls in the hallway to remind you of the historic origins of the building. Both floors have full bathrooms, and two bedrooms occupy the rest of the lower level, while you have the third bedroom and the living room with its open kitchen upstairs. The master bedroom (Bedroom 1) is downstairs, well equipped with a queen size bed and a red chair that accents the artwork on the wall. There won't be any problem with storing your things, as there is storage closet with hangers in addition to another armoire next to the door. The other two bedrooms have queen size beds and storage closets as well. Both bathrooms even have closets in addition to their unique bowl sinks. Upstairs, the kitchen gleams with matching white appliances, including an electric stovetop and oven, microwave and double-doored refrigerator. Turn around and you will be facing the dining and living area, a great place to unwind after a long day. The dining table can seat up to 6, and is also perfect for games or spreading out your NYC map to plan the next day's activities. Two sofa faces each other for winding down, and there is wireless Internet access throughout the duplex. Finally, you have central air conditioning to keep you cool when the weather gets truly sweltering!

With double exposure, the northward facing windows of this apartment overlook the street below, while the southern exposed ones look toward backyard gardens.



Located on 115th Street and Manhattan Avenue, this vacation rental accommodation falls into the Harlem neighborhood of Uptown Manhattan. Greenery is not hard to find around here, with the iconic Central Park just 5 blocks to the south and Morningside Park, a lovely hill-filled terrain with a pond, less than two blocks away. Of course, you can't picnic every day, and that is no problem here with 8th Avenue (Frederick Douglass Boulevard) just around the corner. This thoroughfare has plenty of restaurants and bars, if you have a larger group, the Harlem Tavern is perfect for accommodating with its outdoor patio and serves classic American cuisine and brews, just 2 blocks from your apartment; for something a little more unique, try Africa, an acclaimed restaurant that serves Senagalese fare, also two blocks away, or just stroll down the avenue with an open mind and you'll be sure to find something! For cooking at home, there is a C-Town Supermarket not too far away on 116th Street. Columbia University is also in this part of Harlem, just on the other side of Morningside Park, so keep your eyes open for cultural events that the student population brings to the area!

To navigate the rest of Manhattan, you have two subway stations nearby. The closest is again just one block away on 116th Street and 8th Avenue, serving the B and C lines, which runs down Central Park West and can take you to the Museum of Natural History in just 5 stops, and Columbus Circle in 7! The other subway station is a little further, three longer blocks to the east on 6th Avenue and 116th Street, and serves the 2 and 3 lines that run down Broadway on the Manhattan's west side, and can connect you to the local 1 train or keep you running express all the way to Brooklyn! Experience New York like a native in this beautiful, convenient brownstone apartment.

Guests will also have access to the laundry machines in the building. Did I mention laundry is complimentary with your stay?

We have a full kitchen that guests are welcome to use, with gas stove/oven, dishwasher, full fridge, and microwave.



Hope you dig all night PsyTrance parties! 
Just kidding.

We both have a full time work schedule with hours varying Monday-Friday 5am – 6pm, so during the week you will only really see us at night. We are typically around on the weekends, though sometimes in and out of the apartment. We are of course happy to help guests with any needs they might have.  Plus we can tell you the spots they filmed for Girls! If that's your thing.
 
We are always available via cell phone should you need us. Also the Dog and Cats roam free on the first floor during the day.

BedStuy is a culturally diverse family neighborhood with a strong community bond. Bars, restaurants, and coffee shops are walking distance from the apartment. There is also a beautiful park 3 blocks from the apartment.  It is easy to get to Williamsburg, Downtown Brooklyn, Prospect Park, and the city from our apartment (via public transportation).  We've settled in here quite happily over the last three years.



The apartment is a 10 minute walk to the C train (Kingston & Throop stop), and a 15 minute walk to the express A train (Nostrand Ave stop). The A & C trains will get you into the city in 15 - 20 minutes (1st stop in the city will be Fulton Street). The Brooklyn G train is also close by, 15 minute walk. The bus system is great.  We have the B52 bus that stops across the street from the apartment, which takes you through the neighborhood of Fort Greene, and stops 3 blocks from the Barclays center (walking distance to Park Slope, and downtown Brooklyn). The B43 bus runs north on Throop Ave (at the end of the block) heading into Williamsburg & Greenpoint, and south on Tompkins Ave to take you all the way to Prospect park (West Side). We are happy to provide you with a subway map, and any direction info once you arrive. 

There is always free (parallel) parking in front or around the apartment. 

From JFK, you can take the b15 bus, from 130pl/Bergen road to Lewis av/Gates av and walk 3 blocks. Or a $20 cab. 

From LaGuardia I would recommend a cab, apx $30 - $40. 

From Newark I would recommend a cab, $100 - $120

space: The apartment comes with a full-sized bed in the bedroom and a small couch in the living room, the perfect size for a couple or group of friends. The space is bright and colorful, with a big window in every room and artwork on the walls.
description:
The apartment comes with a full-sized bed in the bedroom and a small couch in the living room, the perfect size for a couple or group of friends. The space is bright and colorful, with a big window in every room and artwork on the walls.

Guests will have access to a fully-equipped kitchen and stocked pantry. For those who like to cook, the apartment has an oven, electric stove, juicer, and Vitamix blender available for use. The dining table seats four. The bathroom has a shower and a full tub, as well as towels and basic toiletries. You will have access to a drawer and an entire closet to hang your clothing in the bedroom. In the living room, there is a desk with a 21" iMac, scanner, and printer for you to use. 

Bonus: I have an extensive collection of design books and nail polishes, if either of those pique your interest. And yes, that's a bear-shaped bean bag chair.

As much or as little as you'd like! I'll certainly be around the neighborhood during your stay. I've lived in the area for almost three years, so I'd be more than happy to recommend places to go and things to do.

Crown Heights is a gem of a neighborhood, bordering tons of other cool neighborhoods like Park Slope, Prospect Heights, and Clinton Hill. There are tons of coffee shops, restaurants, and specialty shops, and at night, you can find dancing and drinks around every corner. On the weekend, take a walk down tree-lined Eastern Parkway to the farmer's market and Prospect Park.

The apartment is located four blocks away from four major subway lines (4,5,2,3), and there are plenty of buses that run close by.

To get to the apartment the airport, I'd recommend taking a taxi (about $45 and 30 minutes from LGA and JFK). If you'd prefer to take the subway, I can send you directions!

If you're traveling with a pup and want some time to explore by yourself or have a date night, I'm available to dog sit during your trip! I'd be more than happy stay home with the dog and take them on a walk while you're out. $50 for the day (6+ hours) and $30 for a partial day (-3 hours).

space:
I'm renting my cute 1 BR apt. Located in the heart of TriBeCa- the most desirable neighborhood in NYC today. The neighborhood is renowned as a foodie haven, home to many of New York's top restaurants (all mins or less walking distance) including DeNiro's TriBeCa Grill, Nobu, Marc Forgione, Tamarind, Locanda Verde, Wolfgang's, The Odeon, Landmarc, Bouley.

Area has drugstores, dry cleaners, shoe repair, everything you need. 5 minute walk to Battery Park on the Hudson River and 5 minute walk to the World Trade center site and the world famous 'Century 21' department store. Near subway stops on 1/2/3 (1 mins), 4/5/6 & N/R (4 mins) and A/C/E (2 mins). 

The apartment’s queen size bed can comfortably fit two people and features a plush down comforter and pillow-top mattress. Apartment also comes with TV, wireless internet, A/C and fully equipped kitchen. Air-conditioning and heat is self-controlled in the apartment.
Laundry room with brand new washers and dryers located at the ground floor.

One last thing... as much as I like kids, the apartment is not child proof and therefore I cannot host kids.

name: Holidays in the Heart of NYC!
summary:
Perfect for exploring the famous Chrismtas Time sites of NYC!

Located in the heart of Midtown, our apartment is a short walk from Central Park, the Rockefeller tree and ice rink, Radio City Music Hall, Bloomingdale's, and more!
space:
Comfortable, functional and well-decorated 1st floor apartment in a classic 1950's NYC style building. Hardwood floors and lots of natural sunlight make for the perfect retreat after a long day exploring the city! Main perks are the convenient location, full kitchen, and sleeping space for up to 5 people to save you money on your trip.

It is a great apartment to explore New York City, with easy access to Central Park, Times Square, Astoria, Brooklyn and all transportation hubs.

=== LOCATION PERKS===

- Low key, safe neighborhood with great bars, restaurants, and lots of shopping nearby (Bloomingdale’s, H&M, Victoria’s Secret, Zara, Sephora, Levi’s, Gap, Banana Republic, Steve Madden, Apple and more!)

- 7 minute walk from 59th St/Lex Ave Subway where you can get on the 4/5/6 and N/Q/R trains. (You can get most places in NYC in under 15-25 minutes from our apartment.)

- 10 minute walk to E/M trains, and 10 minute walk to F train.

- Central Park is 1 mile away, or a 12 minute walk. Great for a picnic or stroll!

- Beautiful grocery store 1 block away (you can stock up and cook your own meals at the apartment to avoid pricey restaurants).

- Easy to grab a cab at any time of day on 1st Ave directly outside of our apartment!

===APARTMENT PERKS===

- Queen size bed with new, very comfortable mattress (sleeps 2)

- Amazing L-shaped couch in a spacious living room (sleeps 1)

- Electric-powered self inflating air mattress available (sleeps 2)

- Lots of natural sunlight throughout apartment

- Functional kitchen with everything you need to cook a feast

- Clean, modern bathroom

- All very well kept, clean floors, tubs, sinks, sheets, etc.

- Lots of coffee making apparatuses, for the coffee making enthusiast (drip machine, keurig, aeropress, pour over, grinder, etc!)

- No elevator, but only one flight up!

- Clean towels and sheets provided

name: Historic Home~Into Manhattan in 20~
space:
Walking distance to the Ferry (6-15 minutes, depending on how fast of a walker you are), take a 20-minute relaxing ferry ride (free) or Express Bus (X13, 14, & 16) into lower Manhattan. The ferry runs every 20 minutes, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; after midnight it runs every hour. Located one block from local and limited bus service and close to above-ground train station. If you prefer to drive, the apartment is located approximately 1.5 miles from the Verrazano Bridge into Bay Ridge, Brooklyn OR approximately 7.5 miles from the Goethals, Outerbridge and Bayonne Bridge into New Jersey.

Located in a Landmark area on a tree-lined, QUIET block in a Quaint/Historic neighborhood one block from the water with restaurants, convenient stores, cozy cafe, fruit/vegetable market within 2 blocks from the apartment. A beautiful park (Clove Lakes Park) with a restaurant on the lake, paddleboats, bicycle path, track, baseball diamond, ice-skating rink, etc. and Silver Lake Golf Course are within close proximity. The St. George Theatre and Farmer's Marker are within walking distance as well. No alternate-side of the street parking :) 3rd floor views of the Statue of Liberty. Charming with all original oak wood trim and updated modern kitchen & baths make this home one of the most sought after homes. Filmed in movies and featured in NY Magazine. 

*Please note, the price is PER ROOM as there are 4 separate rooms in the house. Please see my OTHER LISTINGS for the different rooms available on my profile page. There is AN OPTION TO RENT ALL OF THE ROOMS TO HAVE THE ENTIRE HOME TO YOURSELF. The price for the WHOLE HOME is $350 a night when I am not living there. Please message me and I will send you a special offer for the whole house. Otherwise, when booking each room separately via my other listings there may be others sharing the kitchen and living areas at times similar to a Bed & Breakfast. Still there is quite a bit of room to not feel anyone elses presence :)  Laundry can be done for you on premises for a small fee, but is not for our guest's use, sorry. 

The easiest way to the house is by car service, which you can secure immediately as you depart the airport terminal. 

Please note, this listing, the top room with Statue of Liberty views, will have more pictures soon. We are just about complete with the renovations so updated photos will be coming :)

Please contact Alissa with any questions and interest! 

Also, note, any guests who do not check out promptly by 11a will be charged a $20 late fee for every hour they are late. Unfortunately, we need to implement this now as many people are not honoring the check-out times and our time that we need to get the room and house ready for the next guests. We ask that everyone please be mindful of the check out times so we can be considerate of the next guests. We would be happy to hold luggage for you if your flight takes off later on in the day, but we absolutely need to have the room vacant by 11a. Thanks!

My favorite room in the apartment is the studio/work space with inspiring light and view of the neighborhood. With so much original artwork and personal investment in this space I'm honestly a bit reticent to share it with strangers! summary: Enjoy the best of Brooklyn and Manhattan in this light, roomy two bedroom apartment. With its six windows, three sleeping areas, exposed brick and renovated kitchen and bathroom, its the perfect place to crash after a day of big city fun
space:
We love our roomy two bedroom. Located on a small street full of friendly but quiet neighbors, our place is the perfect place to enjoy the excitement of NYC and the fun of Brooklyn. The building is older and full of character (brick wall, different floorplans), but our apartment is fully renovated (there's even a dishwasher!). 

In addition to the King Sized bed in the master bedroom, the apartment can sleep up to four more people. There is a smaller sleeper sofa in the guest bedroom, and a king-sized sleeper sofa in the main living area. 

The kitchen and the bathroom are both brand new, and there are a total of six windows in the apartment (a New York record? perhaps) that fill the space with great light and cool breezes. 

The guest room also has a large desk in case you're in town to get down to business, literally. The apartment of course has Wifi, and the master bedroom also has a movie/Netflix projector that's ideal for nights in. 

What's ours is yours-- you'll have access to all rooms, etc. We'll even clean out a dresser drawer for you.

While we won't be home while you're there, we'll be reachable. Also, our two best friends live in the building and can be available in a bind. 

Our building straddles the borders of Williamsburg, Bushwick and Bed-Stuy. You'll be surrounded by restaurants, bars, cafes, parks and great people. 

We're two blocks from the Flushing G stop which services Brooklyn and the Flushing J and M stop, which takes you right into lower Manhattan (and beyond). 

What's ours is yours! Plus there's a great rooftop space to enjoy city views 

We won't be home while you're here, but we'll always be available should you have any questions or concerns.

Our building straddles the borders of Williamsburg, Bushwick and Bed-Stuy. You'll be surrounded by restaurants, bars, cafes, parks and great people.

Victorian elegance at its finest with this turn of the century charmer. Full third floor artist (writer, architects) dream studio/work space with incredible light @ 931 square feet. name: Handsome 1BR in Northern Manhattan!
space: If you're planning a trip to New York this holiday season, you should consider staying at our place in the super charming Hudson Heights subsection of Washington Heights in Northern Manhattan.
description:
If you're planning a trip to New York this holiday season, you should consider staying at our place in the super charming Hudson Heights subsection of Washington Heights in Northern Manhattan. 

The apartment is a moderately sized one-bedroom in a handsome pre-war building. It comes complete with a queen size bed, full bathroom, a spacious living room, and an eat-in kitchen. It's a cozy place, fully appointed with comfortable furniture (including a piano and tons of books!) and warm hardwood/parquet floors. The building has washers and driers in the basement. The apartment is fully equipped with high speed Wi-Fi internet.

We like to meet our guests in person during check in and check out, if that's possible. Apart from that, we like to keep a low profile so you can enjoy your privacy during your stay.

Hudson Heights is a lovely neighborhood perched on a bluff overlooking surrounding Washington Heights: it's contains the spot that is at the highest natural elevation on the entire island. The neighborhood is bordered on the South at West 181st Street and the East at Fort Washington Avenue by large cliff faces with impressive, Montmartre-style, outdoor stairways. The Hudson River forms HH's West border, and Fort Tryon Park (with the Cloisters Museum of Medieval Art) forms its Northernmost border. The whole neighbordhood has a lovely, suburban feel, with lots of trees, parks, and beautiful views of the George Washington Bridge, the Henry Hudson river, and New Jersey Palisades. The neighborhood has all the conveniences of living in New York, but it doesn't feel like you're in a big city here. Our apartment is located at the end of a cul-de-sac: since there's no through traffic outside, it's very quiet inside. You could almost forget you're in Manhattan! Probably for this reason, a lot of young couples with babies and students and older people live around here. It's hard not to be charmed by this place.

The immediate surrounding area has some wonderful restaurants and grocery stores (Italian, Irish Pub, sushi, Chinese, Mexican, Russian, American/Southwestern, pizza, Thai, Indian, Tapas, bars, bakeries, diners, access to numerous Latin-American cuisines in nearby Washington Heights, organic and specialty-foods groceries, wine stores, locally owned coffee shops, Starbucks, etc.). There are also a number of nearby churches and synagogues, a Pilates studio, bike trails along the river, and an awesome, independently owned day spa.

The apartment is one block away from the A train, which runs express back and forth from Midtown in about 25 minutes. A few blocks further away, the 1 train runs locally and gets you to Midtown in about 50 minutes. The M98 bus stop (one block away) has almost immediate access to the Harlem-125th Street MetroNorth train station for day-trips to Conncticut, and a blocks beyond that is the nearby George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal for day-trips throughout New Jersey.

As you can see from the pictures of our apartment, we also have a super adorable cat named Noa. If you like cats and don't mind having Noa with you during your visit, we would be happy to offer you a discounted rate on our apartment in exchange for some basic catsitting services. (Noa loves making new friends!) Food and water will be set out and available for him, so all he'll need is a little bit of love. If you're not a fan of cats, or if you'd just prefer to have the place to yourself, we can make plans to have him stay elsewhere during your visit: we have lots of friends and neighbors who can watch him while we're out of the apartment.

summary: There is a private elevator entrance to our spacious, quiet Hamilton Heights 3BR apartment, and this pleasant, sunny room looks out on a row of classic Harlem brownstones.
space:
This bedroom is sunny and quiet and has a closet.  Although the double bed is technically a pull-out sofa, it has a Posturpedic mattress and is extremely comfortable.  
The room fits two people easily, and you'll have your own full bathroom, along with use of the kitchen and living areas.

You will have your own keys, so you can come and go as you please.  We are available to answer questions and help however possible, but the apartment is large, so we won't be in your way.  


Hamilton Heights is a quiet neighborhood of tree-lined streets and striking brownstones, home to plenty of families and students, as well as to the Dance Theater of Harlem, the Society of Arts and Letters, and the historic landmark Hamilton Grange. 
Our favorite neighborhood businesses include the Chipped Cup coffeehouse and Harlem Public, a New York Magazine Critic's Pick. There are also restaurants, grocery stores and pharmacies nearby.    
We are steps away from beautiful Riverside Park, designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, where you can walk or bike along the Hudson while enjoying spectacular views of the George Washington Bridge.  
Also nearby is Riverbank Park, with its huge swimming pool, track and athletic facilities.
We have always felt safe in this neighborhood anytime of day or night. 145th St. Station is a popular stop, so you will never be alone walking along Broadway.  

We are conveniently located 3 minutes walk from the 1 train, and 10 minutes from the A, B, C, and D trains.  Via the subway, it takes 17 minutes to get to Columbus Circle, and 20 minutes to Times Square.  
City College is a 10 minute walk, and Columbia University is an easy 10 minute subway ride away.
There is free, on-street parking on our street and nearby on Riverside Drive.  It is usually easy to find parking within 5 minutes walk of the apartment.  
LaGuardia is the closest airport, about 20 minutes taxi ride away ($35-$50) and also accessible via the M60 bus (transfer to the M101 or M100 on 125th Street). ($2.50)   
For Newark use the AirTrain to access NJTransit and transfer at Penn Station to the NYC Transit. (around $15)  Taxis cost $65-$85 to/from Newark.
For JFK use the AirTrain to access NYC Transit or the Long Island Railroad.  ($7.50-$10)   Taxis cost $50-$75.

summary: Hi!  My name is Patricia.  Thank you for looking at my place. Please read the full description before contacting me to inquire further.  Your questions will most likely be answered here!  Wherever you stay, I hope you enjoy your stay in New York City!
space:
I have lived in the apartment since December of 2012 and I have always loved to have people fill my home, so when a friend suggested that I use this service to meet new people I was overjoyed to learn how easy it was.  Creating a healing and happy environment is something that I like to do so this is a perfect place for me!

Greenpoint is one of the safest, quietest, quaintest, prettiest and most convenient neighborhoods the city has to offer. Five blocks away you have the East River Ferry, which for four dollars will shuttle you directly to Midtown (as well as Williamsburg, Dumbo and Governor’s Island). The G train is less than a 5-minute walk from the location and connections can be made to the L, E, M and 7 trains. All trains are within walking distance. McCarren Park is close by with a large green space, playgrounds, track and a Farmer's Market on Saturdays. If you have a car, parking is relatively easy to find in the neighborhood. Regular alternative side of the street parking rules apply.

There are several new restaurants, bars and coffee shops that have opened up since I have been living here and there is a rich mix of food you can choose from such as Thai, Japanese, Italian, Polish and Korean. On the weekends during the summer the Williamsburg Smorgasboard, a food fair, is within walking distance. There are two yoga studios that take walk in clients and that have a regular daily schedules. There are also at least three grocery stores in the area including an organic market. If you want a spa day, there are tanning salons, nail and waxing shops all around. And right on the corner of my street there is a laundromat that provides laundry service or self service. This place can truly be a home away from home for you!

The apartment has two bedrooms, a living room, a patio and a small bathroom with shelving space available. The kitchen has all the necessary appointments and a small kitchen table that seats 4. The living room has a futon/sofa and a flat screen TV with a DVD player. I have an extensive DVD collection that you may browse and watch including sci-fi/horror, romance, action/adventure and more!

The living room you will be staying in has a full size futon that can comfortably fit two people.  A bath towel, a hand towel and a wash cloth as well as toiletries such as tooth brushes, toothpaste, cotton swabs, body wash and mouth wash are provided as a courtesy for guests and is provided at no additional charge. 

Please note, you will be staying in the common area so please keep this in mind when you make your reservation.  You should not be a light sleeper or have a particular sensitivity to the sound of people walking in and out of the room.

I will be around to give you helpful tips about the neighborhood and to make sure your stay is a pleasant one, however you may see as little or as much of your host as you would like.

I know there is a house rules tab but sometimes people do not look at it so here are the rules:
1) Please no smoking in the house. There is a patio where you may smoke outside.
2) Please no over night guests for more than 1 night unless you have included them in the reservation.
3) No pets are allowed on the premises without express prior approval.
4) Make sure to clean up after yourself immediately after using the kitchen. If you cannot clean up after yourself your kitchen privileges will be revoked.
5) Please take all of your food out of the refrigerator and dispose of it after you leave.
6) You should have something to do outside of the house between the hours of 10 am to 7 pm.  It is not okay to spend full 24 hour cycles on the couch in your pijamas on a regular basis, although on occasion you will be welcome to do so.  You will be staying in the common area of the house so please be mindful of that during the day time hours.  This is not the kind of sleeping arrangement that allows for a peaceful sleep during the day as there will be lots of activity in an out of the apartment during that time. 
7) Since the couch is in a common area, you should keep your personal items tidy and neat.  Please do not leave your clothes and baggage out all over the floor.
8) Checkout is at 11AM on the last day of your stay.

A cleaning/laundry service can be provided on a weekly basis. Please inquire for details when you get here.

space:
Sick location. Conveniently south of Houston at the intersection of King and Macdougal. The sweetest address in all of NYC (1 King St. Apt 1). The location is one of the few truly neighborhood-y places left in Manhattan. Do NYC like a local.

Here's the deal—you get a two floor apartment with high ceilings and exposed brick. A GREAT neighborhood. Super close to w4th station the Houston 1 stop, and Spring CE stops. The entire city is at your front door. Hungry for a cronut? (And patient enough to stand in line?) Dominique Ansel is two blocks away. And your neighbors are famous, which is kinda cool.

I could laundry list all of the rest of the stuff but the key thing about this place is the fact that it's one of the _very_ few places left in lower Manhattan that still feels like a neighborhood. Sure, the kids are partying a couple blocks away above Houston, and the tourists are shopping their sweet asses off in Soho (a few blocks away). But in the six blocks of the South Village there are still amazing things like Raffetto's Pasta which is family owned and has been selling freshly made pasta by the pound since 1903.

The intersection of King and Macdougal boasts seven world class restaurants (hear the buzz lately about Charlie Bird? That's literally on the same block). BUT—it's not a crowded mess of drunk frat kids. Walk a bit north for that, if it's your thing, but then be super stoked that you can just wander a few blocks back to chill.

There's an Apple TV, Wifi, and a Netflix account. I don't have network TV but it's NYC, what're you doing watching television?

You'll have access to the sun-filled open living room and kitchen, including a dining table for 2 and a sofabed that comfortably sleeps 2.  The kitchen features a 4-top gas range and oven, a microwave, and a medium size fridge and freezer, and space in the fridge/freezer and cabinets can be made available on request, although you'll be in the center of New York's dining scene.  

There's a 55" TV with access to Netflix, Hulu, Amazon, and anything else you can get through a Roku, as well as local broadcast TV, and fast wifi.  You're also welcome to use a guest Chromebook laptop - a bit slow, but hey, it came free to me years ago and it's free to you.

You'll also have access to the sunlight-lit full bathroom (combined bathtub/shower), with space in the cabinets below.

Please feel free to peruse the 15 shelves of books as well - just ask if you'd like to borrow for longer than your stay!

While you stay in the living room, I sleep in the bedroom, which is private and off-limits to guests.  

Because I do not have a doorman, I am unable to accept packages or mail for you in advance or during your stay.

As little or as much as desired!  Typically, I leave by 8am on weekdays and return around 8pm.  Aside from morning and evening showers and briefly cooking dinners, I'll be out of your way if you'd like, or around to talk if you'd prefer!

Hell's Kitchen (also called Clinton or Midtown West by realtors) is a fantastic area to live filled with restaurants and bars, and directly adjacent to everything Broadway.  The area definitely caters to adults in their 20s-40s and has a visible LGBT (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender) population, but it's New York - there's a little of everything everywhere.

You're pretty much surrounded by subway lines:

- Columbus Circle (A/C, B/D, 1): 6 min walk
- 50th St & 8th Ave (C/E): 7 min walk
- 55th St & 7th Ave (N/Q/R): 7 min walk
- 53rd St & 7th Ave (B/D, E): 7 min walk
- 57th St & 6th Ave (F): 12 min walk
- Times Square (N/Q/R, S, 1/2/3, 7): 15 min walk

And if you'd prefer to take a taxi, you'll exit the apartment building directly on Ninth Avenue where there are taxis at all hours of the day and night.

There is easy access on mass transit to and from all three NYC airports and both Grand Central Terminal and New York Penn Station.  I'm happy to help suggest easy ways to get in quickly and inexpensively.

For runners and cyclists (bring your own bike or rent a CitiBike less than a block away from the apartment), you're only a couple blocks from the West Side Greenway, a 32-mile long riverside running and biking track that's just about the whole length of Manhattan.

Just another reminder - the building is a walk-up, the apartment is on the fifth floor, and there is no elevator!  I think this is charming and very New York, but you might hate it.

name: Harlem Loft close to Central Park
summary: One bedroom apt featuring lots of sunshine, exposed brick, kitchen with dishwasher, full bath, wireless internet, amazing rooftop. This space is ideal for 1-2 active people (walk up with no elevator) and is half a block from the subway.
space:
Full apartment is available to rent periodically. Please message me if you are interested in the whole apartment. 

Overview
One bedroom apartment featuring lots of sunshine, exposed brick, kitchen with dishwasher, full bath, wireless internet, amazing rooftop with view of Empire State Building, and laundry.  This space is ideal for 1-2 active people (walk up with no elevator!) who want to enjoy the city but come back to a comfortable, relaxed space.   

Location
The apartment is located in a safe part of Harlem very close to a number of trains.  It is 15-20 minutes away from Times Square, Central Park, and many other sites and parks.  It's easy to get to any Manhattan location in about a half hour.  

Safety
I often come home late on the weekends and feel perfectly safe.  The apartment is located 1 block from the 2/3 trains and a couple blocks from the 4/5.  If you are coming back late, I suggest coming home on the 2/3, as it is a shorter walk and well-lit.  

Apartment/ Sleeping arrangements
The apartment is very cute and cozy.  I sleep in the bedroom.  The living room has a pull out sleeping couch that is slightly larger than a twin and also has a loft for sleeping or storage.  A full sized air mattress can be set up in the loft as well.  The living room also has two huge windows and gets so much sunlight that I rarely turn on any lights until the evening.  You have a wonderful view of Harlem from both the apartment and the roof.

Roof
This is the reason I got the apartment!  The roof is beautiful and gets plenty of sunlight even in colder months.  There are deck chairs, a cabana, amazing views of Harlem and all of Manhattan.  It is an absolutely lovely place to drink coffee and read the paper, enjoy a meal, or just take in the city in your own quiet space.

Kitchen/ Breakfast / Meals 
Full kitchen with stove, oven, dishwasher, fridge, kitchen utensils, dishes, and spices to use for cooking.

Bathroom
Full bath available.  Please note that the bathroom is connected to the bedroom so if guests are staying in the living room, they will need to knock.   I am very laid back and respectful and am comfortable sharing my bathroom with guests.  If you need to shower at a specific time please let me know and we will work out a schedule.  

Internet
Wireless internet is available though a bit slow.

Sheets and towels
Bedding and towels will be provided for up to 2 guests.  Please place used towels and sheets in blue hamper when you leave.

Laundry
Washers and dryers are available in the building.  To wash & dry one load costs $2.75.  Laundry detergent is located in the kitchen with all cleaning supplies.

name: Private Room in Crown Heights!
summary: Welcome! We would be happy to host you in our home!
space:
The apartment is located on a busy corner in Crown Heights, Brooklyn.  With people always on the street, day or night, there is never a reason to feel alone!  

The living room is spacious and open with a window that over looks the street.  As the apartment is on a busy corner, one can fully experience the bustling sounds of New York City.  The energetic sunlight and the easy breeze that also flow through the windows makes up for any disturbance that may be caused.   

The available room ( 95ft2/8.9m2) has a very comfortable full-sized bed ( it's more comfortable than my mine.)  The mattress is protected by covers to prevent the infestation of bedbugs. 
In the room, there is a hanging rack behind the door and also a closet with hangers.  The room also has a small table and chair that can be used to work on.  

The kitchen is fully stocked with spices, pots, pans, a stove-- anything one would need to feel at home.  The refrigerator is huge, so yes, there is plenty of space to keep things there.

The bathroom is normal, nothing spectacular, but what is genius about it, is that there will always be clean towels, soap, shampoo and toothpaste! How amazing!

For transportation,  this apartment is a gem because the express "A train" and local "C train"   at Nostrand ave.  and Fulton Street are a quick 3 minute walk.  In the opposite direction, on Eastern Parkway, there is the "3 train", which is a 10 minute walk from home.  
Also, there are plenty of buses to get around Brooklyn and Queens.    

Guests have full access to the kitchen and living room area.  

I'm here!  Ask me questions...

Historically, a Jamaican and Caribbean neighborhood, the cultural ties here are very strong.
